gates.deflated_sharpe: Deflated Sharpe Ratio of the primary rule's active return (strategy minus benchmark, after costs) is at least 0.95
gates.newey_west: Newey–West t-statistic of the primary rule's active return is at least 2
gates.walk_forward: Walk-forward out-of-sample Sharpe beats the benchmark's Sharpe over the same days
gates.holdout: Sharpe over the reserved final 10 years (after costs) is at least the benchmark's
gates.robust: At least 75% of all parameter variants beat the benchmark's Sharpe

trend.benchmark: Buy and hold the US market

quality.benchmark: Buy and hold the US market

ensemble.benchmark: Buy and hold the US market

multifactor.benchmark: Buy and hold the US market

registration.gates_history: Version 1 compared returns with cash; buy-and-hold passes that, so version 2 compares with the benchmark.

data.source: Kenneth R. French Data Library (market, risk-free rate, 12 industries, portfolios on operating profitability, book-to-market and prior 12-2 month return) and FRED DGS10 (10-year Treasury yield, converted to daily par-bond returns)

contamination_note: Industry momentum on this data was already examined in Task 16 (real_world_backtest), and trend-following is widely published, so the reserved final decade is not a pristine holdout. The only clean out-of-sample test is forward paper trading (stage 3).
